events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $5.00 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The driver cancelled and picked rider_no_show in the app, so this is an NS-1/NS-2 case, not NS-3 [F4][NS-0]. Three limbs of NS-1 hold on the system record: arrival was confirmed by the driver's "I'm Here" tap at 09:53:15, 40 m from the pickup, closest approach 37 m [F7][F1][NS-1(i)]; the wait counted from the later of scheduled time and arrival ran 6 min 30 s (390 s), past the 300 s free wait, with no record threshold overriding it [F6][F3][F7][NS-1(ii)][NS-1]; and the driver stayed within 200 m for 7 min 5 s cumulative, stationary at the pickup 09:53:15–09:59:45, with no GPS gap [F2][F3][F6][NS-1(iv)].

The fourth limb fails outright. The timeline records 0 in-app messages and 0 in-app calls before the 09:59:45 cancellation [F5], and the chat record is empty [F10]. NS-1(iii) requires at least one in-app message AND at least one in-app call [NS-1(iii)]. The driver's later written statement that he waited and that the rider no-showed [F11] is a claim, not a message or call, and does not cure the missing contact [NS-1][NS-2].

Because a condition of NS-1 fails, the $5.00 fee is voided and refunded in full [F4][F8][NS-2]. The amount is the fee on record: $5.00 (no distance formula applies in a no-show case). Clean profiles on both sides mean no TH-3 threshold raise and no repeat-fee flag: the rider has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days [F15][NS-9], and the driver's arrival was genuine, so the "fake confirmation" branch of NS-2 is not triggered and no flag_account is due [F7][F1][NS-2]. This matches the driver advocate's own concession and the cited precedent for zero-contact no-show cancellations [F5][F10][F4][PREC-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee to the rider's original payment method; no driver violation or account flag is warranted (arrival was genuine, both profiles clean).

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your no-show cancellation fee. You're getting the $5.00 back, refunded to the same payment method you originally used. Here's what decided it: the driver did arrive and wait past the free wait time, but drivers must also send at least one message and make at least one call through the app before cancelling for a no-show. The records show neither was sent, so the fee doesn't stand. Nothing changes on your account — no flag, and no action needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed the no-show cancellation you filed. The $5.00 no-show fee is being refunded to the rider, so it won't be paid out on this trip. Here's what decided it: your arrival and wait were verified, but cancelling for a no-show also requires at least one message and at least one call through the app beforehand, and the records show neither was sent. No violation or account flag is on your account — your arrival was genuine. No action needed from you.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee to the rider's original payment method; no driver violation or account flag is warranted (arrival was genuine, both profiles clean).
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled and picked rider_no_show in the app, so this is an NS-1/NS-2 case, not NS-3 [F4][NS-0]. Three limbs of NS-1 hold on the system record: arrival was confirmed by the driver's "I'm Here" tap at 09:53:15, 40 m from the pickup, closest approach 37 m [F7][F1][NS-1(i)]; the wait counted from the later of scheduled time and arrival ran 6 min 30 s (390 s), past the 300 s free wait, with no record threshold overriding it [F6][F3][F7][NS-1(ii)][NS-1]; and the driver stayed within 200 m for 7 min 5 s cumulative, stationary at the pickup 09:53:15–09:59:45, with no GPS gap [F2][F3][F6][NS-1(iv)].

The fourth limb fails outright. The timeline records 0 in-app messages and 0 in-app calls before the 09:59:45 cancellation [F5], and the chat record is empty [F10]. NS-1(iii) requires at least one in-app message AND at least one in-app call [NS-1(iii)]. The driver's later written statement that he waited and that the rider no-showed [F11] is a claim, not a message or call, and does not cure the missing contact [NS-1][NS-2].

Because a condition of NS-1 fails, the $5.00 fee is voided and refunded in full [F4][F8][NS-2]. The amount is the fee on record: $5.00 (no distance formula applies in a no-show case). Clean profiles on both sides mean no TH-3 threshold raise and no repeat-fee flag: the rider has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days [F15][NS-9], and the driver's arrival was genuine, so the "fake confirmation" branch of NS-2 is not triggered and no flag_account is due [F7][F1][NS-2]. This matches the driver advocate's own concession and the cited precedent for zero-contact no-show cancellations [F5][F10][F4][PREC-1].

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) before cancelling, the driver sent ≥ 1 in-app message AND made ≥ 1 in-app call), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The $5.00 no-show fee cannot stand because NS-1(iii) fails outright: the driver sent zero in-app messages and made zero in-app calls before cancelling at 09:59:45.

The chat record is complete and empty — no in-app chat messages exist between rider and driver — so the driver's written statement that he waited, made after the trip, is the only support for contact, and RD-5/NS-1 require an actual message and call, not the driver's word.
Any NS-1 failure voids the fee in full: the record shows the driver picked reason rider_no_show in the app and charged $5.00, so under NS-2 the rider is entitled to refund_full of $5.00.

The driver did stay at/near the pickup point (arrival 09:53:15 and 6 min 30 s inside 200 m), but that condition alone is not enough — NS-1 requires the message and call conditions cumulatively, and those are unmet.

The complaint's account is consistent with the system record: the driver cancelled at 09:59:45 without any contact attempt, and the rider says she arrived about a minute later, so no showing-up failure can be inferred from the records available.
The rider has no upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days, so NS-9 flagging is not engaged and no repeat-rider penalty applies here.
A recent precedent on the same clause, DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel with zero contact), confirms the $5.00 fee does not stand where the driver made no contact attempt.

weaknesses: The driver did press "I'm Here" at 09:53:15 and stayed within 200 m for 6 min 30 s (F6, F7, F2), so NS-1(i) and (iv) are arguably satisfied and the wait condition (ii) passed on the record's timing (F4, F6) — the driver will argue the only shortfall is formal contact, which the other side may try to supplement with his statement in F11.

The rider's own account that she came down about a minute after cancellation is a statement, not a system record; there is no GPS or message record proving where she was at 09:53–09:59, so the driver may argue she was not available during the wait.

claims.assertion: The driver arrived at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 37 m and he tapped "I'm Here" at 09:53:15 while 40 m from the pickup point, satisfying the arrival limb of NS-1(i).

The driver was continuously at the pickup point: he was stationary from 09:53:15 to 09:59:45 (6 min 30 s) at 40 m from the pickup, within 200 m for 7 min 5 s cumulatively, so NS-1(iv) is met with no GPS gap to escalate on.

The free wait was satisfied: counted from the later of scheduled pickup and recorded arrival (09:53:15), the driver waited 6 min 30 s before cancelling at 09:59:45, past the 5-minute free wait in NS-1(ii).

The driver cancelled for rider no-show and not for a reason of his own: the app reason recorded is rider_no_show and his statement records waiting past five minutes before cancelling, so NS-0 routes this to NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3.

The rider's own complaint places them away from the pickup for the whole wait, saying only that they came downstairs a minute after the cancellation, while no chat record exists on either side (0 messages, 0 calls) and the trip was a plain 1.0x fare with no surge or traffic issue.

Both parties' profiles are clean, so there is no fraud or repetition ground to raise the confidence threshold or to add a flag: the rider has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days and the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld across 910 trips.

weaknesses: NS-1(iii) fails on the undisputed system records: before cancelling the driver sent 0 in-app messages and made 0 in-app calls (F5), and the chat record is empty (F10), so the fee is likely voided under NS-2 on that condition alone and $5.00 refunded.
The rider's complaint that he was never messaged or called is corroborated by the timeline (F5) and will be read as evidence for the rider.

The driver's statement that he 'waited more than 5 minutes' (F11) is a statement only; it adds nothing to the GPS and timeline facts (F3, F6) and cannot cure the missing contact requirement of NS-1(iii).

points.response: Conceded: the driver did arrive — 37 m closest approach and an "I'm Here" tap at 40 m (F1, F7) — so NS-1(i) is satisfied; this does not save the fee because NS-1 requires all four conditions.
Conceded: he was stationary 09:53:15–09:59:45 at 40 m with no GPS gap (F3, F2), so NS-1(iv) is met and there is nothing to escalate under TH-4; the defect lies elsewhere.
Conceded: measured from recorded arrival 09:53:15 the wait was 6 min 30 s, so NS-1(ii) is satisfied (F6, F3); again, satisfaction of one limb does not carry the others.
Conceded only as a routing point: the app reason is rider_no_show (F4), so NS-0 sends this to NS-1/NS-2 — but NS-1 is a four-limb test and the fee stands only if every limb holds.

Misread: F5 and F10 are the rider's best facts, not the driver's — the timeline records 0 in-app messages and 0 in-app calls before cancellation and the chat record is empty, so NS-1(iii) fails on undisputed system records; the rider's absence during the wait is not proven by any record, and the empty chat cuts against the driver because it is he who must show the message and the call. F9, F12, F13 and F14 (1.0x, no congestion, fair weather) are irrelevant to NS-1(iii) and add nothing to the driver's case.

Accepted, but it is neutral: clean profiles on both sides (F15, F16) mean no TH-3 threshold raise and no flag_account or NS-9 add-on — the fee is voided simply because NS-1(iii) was never performed, and NS-2 requires refund_full whenever any NS-1 condition fails.

Conceded on the condition itself: the system timeline shows 0 in-app messages and 0 in-app calls before the 09:59:45 cancellation (F5) and the chat record is empty (F10), so NS-1(iii) is not met and NS-2 voids the $5.00.

Conceded that the driver's written statement (F11) cannot stand in for the message and call NS-1(iii) requires; my client's statement is not a call recording and NS-1 treats verbal contact as needing recorded evidence, so on contact the record is against us.

Conceded in outcome: since NS-1(iii) fails, NS-2 requires refund_full of the $5.00 charged on the record (F8) — note however that the amount is the fee, not a distance fare, and no flag_account is warranted because the driver's arrival was genuine (F3, F7) and both profiles are clean (F15, F16).

I agree the arrival and wait conditions are met on the system record (F3, F6, F7, F2), which is exactly why NS-1(i), (ii) and (iv) are not in dispute; only the contact condition fails, and NS-1 speaks of conditions holding cumulatively.

The rider's statement about arriving a minute later is not a system record — there is no GPS or message record of the rider's position during 09:53–09:59 — but it does not matter: the fee fails on the driver's own contact record (F5, F10) regardless of when the rider came down.
I do not contest this: the rider has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F15), so NS-9 flagging is not engaged against the rider, and equally nothing in the driver's profile engages RD-6 or a flag (F16).

The precedent they cite bears on a genuine no-show cancellation with zero contact (F5, F10, F4); my client arrived, tapped "I'm Here" 40 m from the pickup and stayed 6 min 30 s (F7, F3), so only the contact limb of NS-1 is breached and the refund is limited to the $5.00 fee under NS-2.
